title: Information on Public Sector Corruption Cases in 2016
what_it_is: Information on Public Sector Corruption Cases in 2016

sections.label: CPIB corruption statistics 2016
sections.summary: CPIB registered 118 cases for investigation in 2016, 15% from the public sector, averaging about 14% over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: According to CPIB's corruption statistics that were released recently, there were 118 cases registered for investigation in 2016, out of which, 15% was from the public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The percentage of public sector cases that CPIB registered for investigation remains consistent over the last three years, averaging about 14%.

sections.label: CPIB prosecutions and bribe amounts
sections.summary: In 2016 CPIB prosecuted 104 individuals, four public sector employees, with total bribe amount involving public servants at $24,800.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In 2016, there were 104 individuals who were prosecuted in Court by the CPIB, out of which, four were public sector employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: To answer Mr Png's question, the total bribe amount, or personal gains involving public servants prosecuted last year was $24,800.

sections.label: Uncompleted cases over two years
sections.summary: In 2016, 13 of the 92 uncompleted cases carried forward from 2015 took more than two years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For 2016, there were 13 cases from the 92 uncompleted cases that were carried forward from 2015 that took more than two years.

sections.label: Singapore corruption rankings 2016
sections.summary: Transparency International ranked Singapore seventh least corrupt in 2016, and it kept first place in the PERC survey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index 2016 ranks Singapore as the seventh least corrupt country in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Singapore has also maintained its first place in the 2016 Political and Economic Risk Consultancy Annual Survey on corruption.

sections.label: Factors deciding prosecution
sections.summary: Which case will be prosecuted depends on the case's nature, evidence strength, complexity and severity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The second question as to which case will be prosecuted will depend on the nature of the case itself and also the strength of the evidence, the complexity and the severity of the case.
